summary: Janice Leoshko is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She completed her doctoral studies under Susan L. Huntington and became Professor Emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin, attested in 2026.

Jann Ronis is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under David Germano, having also studied under Jeffrey Hopkins and Sonam Tenpa, and held a post there attested in 2007.
Jared Rhoton (1941–1993) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his dissertation at Columbia University in 1985 under Alex Wayman and also studied under Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga.

Jarl Charpentier (1884–1935) was a Swedish Indologist and linguist. He studied at Uppsala University and the University of Bonn, working at Uppsala as Assistant Professor (1908), Deputy Professor (1925), and Professor from 1927, succeeding Karl Ferdinand Johansson.

Jaromír Borecký (1869–1951) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at the Faculty of Arts, Charles University in Prague (~1888–1893) and later served as Director of the National Library of the Czech Republic (~1920–1935).

Jaromír Jedlička (1869–1901) specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Charles University (1888–1894), completing his PhD under Josef Zubatý, and worked as a library worker at Charles University in 1899.
Jaroslav Průšek (1906–1980) was a sinologist who studied at Charles University's Faculty of Arts around 1924–1928.

Jason Birch is an Indologist who earned his D.Phil. at the University of Oxford (2008–2013) under Alexis Sanderson. He served as Senior Research Fellow at SOAS (2015–2024) and Research Associate at Oxford (2024).

Jason Hawkes is a scholar of archaeology and Indology who earned his PhD from Cambridge (2002–2008). He held posts at Cambridge, the British Museum (2014–2020), and Gonville and Caius College (2021), among others.

Jason M. Wirth (born 1963) works in philosophy, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Kosho Itagaki (attested 2017–2019) and was appointed Professor at Seattle University in 2005.

Jason Matthew McCombs is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles in 2014 under Gregory Schopen, later serving as a lecturer there.

Jason Neelis works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Washington (1992–2001) under Richard G. Salomon and became an Associate Professor at Wilfrid Laurier University in 2010.

Jason Protass specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at Stanford University under John Kieschnick (attested 2015–2016) and held positions as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University and Fulbright Fellow at Academia Sinica.

Javana Ñāṇa specializes in Buddhist studies. Having studied at the National University of Mongolia, ITBMU, SSBU, and the University of Kelaniya, he held an appointment as Bhikkhu at Shan State Buddhist University in 2025.

Jay Holt Valentine specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Virginia (2004–2013) under Kurtis R. Schaeffer and was appointed Associate Professor at Troy University in 2015.

Jay Jasanoff (born 1942) is a linguist and Indologist. An alumnus of Harvard University, he served as full professor at Cornell (1981–1985) before returning to Harvard in 1998 as Diebold Professor of Indo-European Linguistics and Philology.

Jay L. Garfield (born 1955) works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Hampshire College, the University of Melbourne, and the National University of Singapore, later becoming Doris Silbert Professor Emeritus at Smith College.
Jayadevbhai Mohanlal Shukla is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar and served as Reader of Sanskrit at Gujarat University.

Jayandra Soni (born 1947) works in Indology and philosophy. He earned PhDs from Banaras Hindu University (~1975–1978) and McMaster University (~1980–1987), later serving as a Lecturer at the University of Marburg (1991–2012).

Jayanta Acharya is an Indology scholar who completed a PhD at Nepal Sanskrit University (2018–2022). He became a Professor at Nepal Sanskrit University in 1997 and served as a SPOCS with the International Astronomical Union (2009–2018).
